title: The Horizon of Mount Kessler
premise: Yara Zhou has spent a decade erasing themselves from their famous archaeologist mother's shadow, guiding treks through the Kessler Range where no one asks questions. When prospector Elias Vann dies in Yara's camp, he leaves a map to a pre-colonial highland city and a dying request: bring it home before the monsoon seals the passes. Yara assembles a ragtag expedition—Vann's estranged granddaughter, a disgraced surveyor, and a porter with his own debts—and discovers the 'city' is also evidence of a massacre covered up by the mining consortium that funded Yara's mother's career. Racing weather and a consortium fixer sent to bury the site forever, Yara must choose between loyalty to the crew who trusted them and the truth that will burn every bridge back to their old life. The expedition reaches the valley days before landfall; they document everything, smuggle the evidence out by river, and Yara finally goes public—estranged from the past, but no longer invisible.
about_author: Wren Okafor is a former field guide turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot. They live between seasons, splitting the year between a mountain town and wherever the research takes them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Silence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Leading a supply trek through the Kessler foothills, Yara deflects a client's questions about their mother, the celebrated archaeologist Dr. Mei-Lin Zhou. Beat: competence masking loneliness—we see how carefully Yara has built an unremarkable life.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Fire
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A half-dead prospector, Elias Vann, stumbles into camp raving about a green valley above the ice line. Yara patches him up against their better judgment. Beat: reluctant compassion—the first crack in Yara's isolation.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Vann's POV (final hours). Knowing he won't last the night, Vann trades Yara his map for a promise: take it up the mountain, don't sell it, don't give it to the consortium men who killed his partner. Beat: a burden accepted under oath.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Studying Vann's map, Yara recognizes survey marks matching their mother's old field notes—meaning the consortium knew decades ago. A fixer named Corrigan arrives asking after Vann. Beat: dread; invisibility is ending.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Nadia Vann's POV. In the lowland town of Harrow Bend, Nadia—estranged from her grandfather for years—learns of his death and that a stranger holds his map. She confronts Yara in a dockside bar. Beat: grief weaponized into demand.

chapters.title: Terms of Ascent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara offers Nadia a place on the climb instead of a fight, and recruits disgraced surveyor Tomas Reyes and porter Bektour, each carrying debts of their own. Beat: a found family assembling out of necessity, not trust.

chapters.title: Corrigan's Offer
chapters.summary: Corrigan's POV. The consortium fixer makes Yara a generous offer to hand over the map, hinting he knows exactly who Yara's mother is—and what happened at Site Nine. Beat: temptation with teeth; the past knocking.

chapters.title: The Ice Line
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The team crosses onto the glacier; a crevasse nearly takes Bektour, saved by Nadia's quick rope work. First real bonding around the stove that night. Beat: fear transmuted into fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Radio reports put the monsoon two weeks early. Tomas calculates they have eleven days to reach the valley and get out. Corrigan's team is spotted on their trail. Beat: the clock starts; stakes sharpen.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A rockfall blocks the high pass; the team must risk the exposed traverse Vann's map warns about. Nadia reveals she read her grandfather's letters—she knew what he was looking for all along. Beat: honesty as survival.

chapters.title: Site Nine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV (flashback interwoven). At a ruined waystation, Yara finally tells Nadia the truth: as a teenager, Yara found bones at Site Nine and was made to sign a silence agreement by their mother's funders. Beat: confession; the theme of justice outside the law crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Green Valley
chapters.summary: Bektour's POV. They descend into the hidden valley and find it: terraces, standing stones, a city older than any record. Bektour, whose village was flooded by a consortium dam, understands instantly what this place means. Beat: awe braided with anger.

chapters.title: The Massacre Wall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the great hall, murals record a colonial-era slaughter—and the consortium's original survey photos, cached by Vann, prove the company knew and built over it. Beat: proof in hand; now the question is what proof is for.

chapters.title: Corrigan Arrives
chapters.summary: Corrigan's POV. His team enters the valley under white flags and offers the crew triple pay and quiet futures. Tomas wavers; Bektour refuses flatly. Beat: loyalty tested with money instead of violence.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Overnight, Corrigan's men cut the ropes at the exit traverse and destroy the radio. One of their own porters defected. Someone will not make it down if they move fast on bad anchors. Beat: betrayal; the adventure turns lethal.

chapters.title: The Descent Decision
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With six days to landfall and one safe route, Yara proposes splitting: the evidence goes out fast with the lightest climbers while the rest hold the valley and document everything. Nadia volunteers for the fast team. Beat: leadership earned; sacrifice chosen.

chapters.title: White Water
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The fast team runs the melt-swollen river gorge on a raft lashed from tent poles, losing the duplicate negatives but keeping the originals sealed in oilskin. Beat: terror and exhilaration; the plan working by inches.

chapters.title: Hold the Valley
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Below, Corrigan tries to burn the murals; Yara and Bektour drive the crew off but Bektour takes a fall protecting the wall. Monsoon clouds swallow the rim. Beat: the cost of standing ground.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The monsoon hits. Trapped together in the great hall, Yara and Corrigan finally talk honestly—he was at Site Nine too, a young man following orders. Beat: enemy humanized; the cycle of complicity named.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. After the storm breaks, the whole team descends the eastern route Vann marked, carrying Bektour on a litter, leaving the valley undocumented to satellites but documented in their own hands. Beat: endurance; family carrying its wounded.

chapters.title: Everything We Found
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. In Harrow Bend, Nadia releases the evidence to journalists and the national archive simultaneously; Yara stands beside their mother at the press conference, telling the whole story including Site Nine. Beat: truth over loyalty to blood or employers; catharsis.

chapters.title: The Horizon of Mount Kessler
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. Months later, the valley is a protected site run with descendant communities; Bektour walks again, Tomas has his license back, Nadia leads the first academic season. Yara guides one last private trek—not hiding anymore, just home. Beat: quiet resolution; the wilderness forgave nothing, and that was the point.
